Urban Company has launched its qualified institutional placement (QIP), setting the floor price at Rs 161.03 per share, as the home services platform looks to raise capital amid continued investment in its business expansion.

The company may offer institutional investors a discount of up to 5 per cent on the floor price, following shareholder approval for the pricing flexibility. The final issue price will be decided in consultation with the book-running lead managers.
In a regulatory filing on Monday, Urban Company said its Fund Raise Committee had approved the opening of the QIP and the Preliminary Placement Document at a meeting held on 16 November.

The fundraising exercise follows the board’s approval on 16 October and a special resolution passed by shareholders through a postal ballot on 15 November. The company will submit the placement document to the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) and BSE.
Urban Company has also closed its trading window until further notice in connection with the issue, in compliance with insider trading regulations.

The capital raise comes at a time when Urban Company’s expansion strategy is putting pressure on its bottom line. The company reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 182.5 crore in Q2FY27, sharply higher than the Rs 59 crore loss recorded in the corresponding quarter last year.

Revenue grew at a healthier pace, rising 41.4 per cent year on year to Rs 537.3 crore from Rs 380 crore. However, the company’s EBITDA loss widened to Rs 187.6 crore from Rs 68.4 crore a year earlier, reflecting continued spending on its InstaHelp business.
Urban Company said its core business continued to grow while delivering an improvement in margins. It also reported better unit economics in InstaHelp as the service expanded.
The QIP will provide the company with an opportunity to raise fresh institutional capital as it balances investments in newer services with the need to improve overall profitability.
